changes: Terminal capture-state events request a coalesced read after all active cleanup has ended. No timer added.
In-flight results that predate cleanup or a connection change are discarded; busy foreground tasks defer reads until snapshot completion.
Results publish on the Qt owner thread. Remaining monitor interfaces are not assumed owned by their names.
Refresh preserves real error and stopping badges; failed reads publish unknown rather than idle.
Successful capture-result pulls retain the shared SFTP session; network IO failures dispose it through its connection owner.
Batch AP rename titles display the configured owning radio band; unresolved bands are labelled unknown.
Visible file panes also refresh after capture cleanup. Requests wait for ongoing file operations or hidden-page reentry, coalesce, and discard old-device requests; subscriptions detach on disposal.

five_ghz.existing_fix: ap_startup_wait + ap_dfs_observation are already shared by save/apply, direct toggle and recovery. No DFS implementation changed in this turn.
five_ghz.limits: 60-second CAC can exceed the old 45-second wait. Existing native rollback bounds remain enforced; log recognition and live AP-ready proof are required.

Real conflict, stopping and error states remain visible; unknown probe outcomes do not assert idle.
